name: Relative Initial-Ideal Maximum-Parent Criterion
statement: Fix visible class $C$, auxiliary mark $\tau$, total coordinate set of size $N$, and rank $r$. A coordinate-multigraded ideal $F$ with the maximum-class Hilbert series $\mathcal H_{N,r}$ and exact marked colon $(F:m_\tau)\cap S_X=Q_C$ exists exactly when $C$ has a rank-$r$ maximum parent at that mark. For a block term order placing every opposite auxiliary literal before all monomials without one, $\operatorname{in}(F)=Q_M$ for such a parent and its marked colon remains $Q_C$.
proof: The prescribed Hilbert series forces the initial ideal to contain no monomial on at most $r$ colors and exactly one signed squarefree monomial on each $(r+1)$-support. Full-word counting gives the Sauer cardinality and the selected patterns bound VC dimension, so their avoider is rank-$r$ maximum. Homogeneous polarization then gives equality of the whole initial ideal with its signed ideal. Under the elimination block order, a leading monomial compatible with the mark comes from a polynomial containing no opposite auxiliary literal; coordinate homogeneity factors its marked auxiliary part, and the prescribed colon forces the visible leading factor into $Q_C$. This preserves the exact marked colon. The converse takes $F=Q_M$.
